pathways.name: TGF-β / Fibrosis Pathway
pathways.description: The central profibrotic pathway in SSc. TGF-β1 produced by macrophages, fibroblasts, and endothelial cells binds TGFBR1/TGFBR2, activating SMAD2/3 phosphorylation. pSMAD2/3 complexes with SMAD4 to drive transcription of collagen (COL1A1, COL1A2), fibronectin, CTGF, and α-SMA (myofibroblast marker). Sustained TGF-β signaling drives the hallmark fibrosis of skin and internal organs in SSc. PPARγ normally antagonizes TGF-β/SMAD but is downregulated in SSc.

pathways.name: Endothelin / Vasculopathy Pathway
pathways.description: Endothelin-1 (EDN1) is a potent vasoconstrictor and profibrotic peptide overproduced by dysfunctional SSc endothelial cells. EDN1 binds ETA (vasoconstriction, smooth muscle proliferation) and ETB (vasodilation, ET-1 clearance) receptors on vascular smooth muscle. PDE5 degrades cGMP, limiting NO-mediated vasodilation. Prostacyclin (PGI2) via IP receptor promotes vasodilation. sGC stimulators enhance cGMP production. This pathway drives PAH, digital ulcers, Raynaud's, and scleroderma renal crisis in SSc.

pathways.name: IL-6 / JAK-STAT Signaling
pathways.description: IL-6 is a central cytokine in SSc driving both inflammation and fibrosis. Elevated in SSc serum, skin, and BAL fluid, IL-6 signals through the IL-6R/gp130 complex activating JAK1/JAK2 → STAT3. Phosphorylated STAT3 directly induces collagen and TIMP-1 expression in fibroblasts. STAT4 (risk gene) mediates IL-12/IL-23 → Th1/Th17 polarization. The IL-6/STAT3 axis drives the Th17/Treg imbalance and myofibroblast persistence characteristic of SSc.
therapeutic_targets: Potential: JAK inhibitors (tofacitinib, baricitinib under investigation for SSc)

pathways.name: B Cell Dysregulation & Autoantibody Production
pathways.description: B cell dysregulation is a hallmark of SSc, with polyclonal B cell activation, memory B cell expansion, and production of disease-defining autoantibodies (anti-Scl-70, anti-centromere, anti-RNA pol III). BAFF promotes B cell survival and autoreactive B cell escape. BLK, BANK1, and FCGR2B regulate BCR signaling thresholds. IL-21 from Tfh cells drives B cell differentiation. CD20+ B cell infiltration in SSc skin correlates with fibrosis severity, and B cells produce profibrotic IL-6.

pathways.name: Innate Immune / TLR4 Signaling
pathways.description: Innate immune activation through TLRs is a key upstream driver of SSc. TLR2 and TLR4 recognize endogenous DAMPs released from damaged endothelial cells and apoptotic debris. TLR activation in plasmacytoid dendritic cells and macrophages drives IRF5/IRF8-mediated type I IFN production. In fibroblasts, TLR4 ligation directly induces TGF-β, IL-6, and collagen. TNFAIP3 (A20) and TNIP1 normally limit TLR/NF-κB signaling; their genetic variants impair this negative regulation. DNASE1L3 deficiency leads to accumulation of TLR9-stimulatory DNA.

pathways.name: T Cell Autoimmunity & Costimulation
pathways.description: T cell dysregulation in SSc includes Th2/Th17 skewing, Treg dysfunction, and Tfh expansion. CD247 (CD3ζ) variants impair TCR signaling. TNFSF4 (OX40L) enhances T cell costimulation and survival. STAT4 drives Th1/Th17 polarization. IL-12A promotes Th1 responses. PTPN22 regulates TCR/BCR signaling thresholds. Activated T cells infiltrate SSc skin and produce IL-4, IL-13 (Th2), and IL-17 (Th17), which directly stimulate fibroblast collagen production and promote the Th2-fibrosis axis.
therapeutic_targets: T cell costimulation blockers (abatacept, off-label use in SSc)
